brief: A salad staircase against a sunny kitchen wall: three rows of three planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back, so the back row does not shade the front. Lettuce seedlings in the front row, young lettuce in the middle row and full-size romaine at the back. Fill every planter with soil and plant it.

requirements.evidence: 3x3 footprint levels 0-2: front row r=1 level 0 only (1 storey), middle rows r=0 levels 0-1 (2 storeys), back rows r=-1 levels 0-2 (3 storeys); staircase steps up back.
requirements.requirement: Three rows of three stepping 1, 2, 3 storeys front to back

requirements.evidence: bins bin:-1,1,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:1,1,0 (front) + bins middle/back; 9 full-depth bins total
fillSoil on all 9 bins via fill_and_plant; check_build no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL
requirements.requirement: Fill every planter with soil and plant it

finish.summary: Salad staircase: 3x3 bases stepping 1/2/3 storeys front-to-back, 9 full bins with soil, romaine seedlings front, young middle, harvest-size romaine back. Caps, joints, mesh clear; plants visible from front and above.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
